relevance_note: The paper's own multicenter cohort includes HA20 patients with TNFAIP3 variants ('nine patients (from six unrelated families) in the study were diagnosed with HA20'), but they are described only in aggregate, with per-patient clinical data referred to supplementary Table S2, which is not in this text.
method_note: Read the whole Markdown manually; no script transcribed any table (a script only assembled the JSON). Flag set to true because the paper reports nine HA20 patients from its own study whose TNFAIP3 variants were determined; however, the main text gives no label, sex, age, phenotype or genotype for any individual HA20 patient (per-patient data are only in supplementary Table S2, not available here), so the individuals, variants, phenotypic_features and phenotype_checklist tables are left empty rather than inventing unlabeled people. Two TNFAIP3 variants are named ('two variants (p.Lys329Asn*1 and p.Gly583*) newly confirmed to be pathogenic using a NF-κB reporter gene activity assay') but neither is attributed to a patient or family, so no variants rows were emitted; the 'several previously reported variants (32)' are not listed. The Discussion says variants of unknown significance were found in TNFAIP3 'as in the present study' without saying in whom. Patients P1-P19 in Table 2 are undiagnosed patients with high IFN scores, none with a reported TNFAIP3 variant (P1 has PSMB8 compound heterozygous mutations; P2, P3, P4 and P6 have a 'Possibly pathogenic variant found in WES' in unnamed genes), so they were excluded as outside the HA20 scope. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients = true refers only to non-HA20 patients 7 and 11 (refs 34, 35); the paper does not state whether any HA20 patient was published before (ref 32 is cited for variants, not explicitly for the same patients). Contradictions noted (none affect HA20 data): the abstract says '117 samples from 94 patients' while Methods say 'Samples were collected from a total of 117 individuals'; Table 1 gives 'Male | 7/19 | (36.8) | 6/13 | (35.3)', where 6/13 does not equal 35.3%; Table 2's two header rows are misaligned with the data columns.
